sources.title: Leaving No One Behind at Local Level: Cabo Delgado Province Report
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), Mozambique; Government of Mozambique
sources.temporal_coverage: Local fieldwork May–June 2023; report published September 2025; climate-shock findings include Cyclone Kenneth (2019) and prior analysis through 2021.
sources.methodology: Review of provincial/district statistics and documents; interviews and survey involving 148 people in Cabo Delgado.
sources.limitations: District selection considered poverty, security and accessibility; findings are not representative of the whole province. Some climate-conflict statements summarize cited prior reports.

sources.title: Mozambique Humanitarian Situation Report No. 12 (End of Year), 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation and UNICEF response reporting for January–December 2025; report published 9 February 2026.
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational reporting drawing on government, partner, displacement and service-delivery data.
sources.limitations: Operational report, not an independent impact evaluation; needs and partner-reported outputs may be incomplete. Historical 2025 results are not current 2026 conditions.

sources.title: United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework Evaluation: Mozambique (2025), Final Report
sources.organization: United Nations Sustainable Development Group; independent evaluation team
sources.temporal_coverage: Evaluation of 2022–2026 Cooperation Framework; findings mainly cover 2022–2025; field visits and interviews in August–September 2025.
sources.methodology: Independent evaluation using document review, surveys, interviews, focus groups and site visits, with triangulation.
sources.limitations: Fieldwork focused on Maputo, Gaza and Niassa and synthesized some parallel agency evaluations; time, selection, recall and institutional biases remain possible.

sources.title: Comunidades de Cabo Delgado Validam Planos de Acção Espacial
sources.organization: United Nations in Mozambique; Cabo Delgado Provincial Government; UN-Habitat and partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Community planning release dated 26 August 2026; plans and near-term actions described at publication.
sources.methodology: Official UN release describing a participatory territorial-planning process and selected communities.
sources.limitations: Press release reports planned measures and stated tension risks, not an evaluation of implementation or outcomes.

sources.limitations: Brief official meeting report; no district-level population denominator or climate-change attribution is supplied.

sources.title: Presidente do INGD destaca a importância da antecipação durante o balanço da época chuvosa 2025/2026 em Moçambique
sources.organization: National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD), Mozambique
sources.temporal_coverage: INGD review of the 2025–2026 rainy and cyclone season; anticipatory actions reported for December 2025–March 2026; page published 13 August 2026.
sources.methodology: Official summary by the INGD president of seasonal review findings and anticipatory-action results presented to government and partners.
sources.limitations: Aggregated agency-reported results; the release does not disaggregate evacuations or warning reach by named district or establish a counterfactual.

claims.paraphrase: In the Chiúre–Mecúfi–Pemba study sample, 56.1% reported Cyclone Kenneth impacts; over half of those affected were already displaced. The report describes weak housing and sanitation as compounding exposure.
claims.limitations: Survey findings are local and refer to 2019 cyclone impacts; the report does not attribute this event to anthropogenic climate change.

claims.paraphrase: UNDP's review cites earlier analysis that conflict-driven flight from homes and fields coincided with erratic-rainfall crop losses; displaced fishers also shifted to unfamiliar subsistence farming.
claims.limitations: The climate–food-security passage summarizes a cited OCHA 2022 analysis; it is historical and does not estimate a causal effect on violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report states that conflict displacement and erratic rainfall jointly worsen food insecurity through loss of homes, fields and normal production.

claims.locator: PDF p.1 (printed p.1), Situation Overview; PDF p.2 (printed p.2), conflict and cyclone displacement details.
claims.paraphrase: In 2025, conflict drove major displacement from Memba District, Nampula: over 112,000 people fled, 65% children. Separately, about 15% of IDPs were in Sofala, mainly after climate shocks.
claims.limitations: The report distinguishes conflict-driven northern displacement from climate-related displacement in Sofala; do not merge these drivers.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report says conflict displacement and climate shocks compound humanitarian vulnerability, but does not say climate caused the armed conflict.

claims.locator: PDF p.1 (printed p.1), Situation Overview; p.2, Health and HIV/AIDS response.
claims.paraphrase: Dikeledi and Jude affected over 1.3 million people in Q1 2025, mostly in Nampula, damaged 131 health facilities and 3,128 classrooms, and disrupted learning for 365,000-plus students.
claims.limitations: The report records event impacts but does not attribute individual cyclones to climate change.

claims.locator: PDF pp.1–2 (printed pp.1–2), Health and Nutrition response; p.4, WASH coordination.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF deployed 3,924 mobile teams across 1,556 communities and resettlement sites; integrated brigades served hard-to-reach conflict- or climate-shock-affected areas in five named provinces.
claims.limitations: Reported 2025 activity and reach are operational outputs, not proof of sustained resilience or independent effectiveness.

claims.locator: PDF pp.64–65 (printed pp.61–62), Finding 19; PDF pp.65–68 (printed pp.62–65), Findings 20–22.
claims.paraphrase: Evaluation finds humanitarian access in insecure northern districts constrained by conflict and instability; activity and staff training were interrupted in Cabo Delgado, while mobile brigades and boat clinics adapted delivery.
claims.limitations: Evaluation synthesized programme reporting; fieldwork concentrated in Maputo, Gaza and Niassa, so north-specific detail is uneven.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The evaluation explicitly identifies northern insecurity and conflict as constraints on humanitarian reach and continuity.

claims.paraphrase: The evaluation reports 268 local disaster-risk committees trained, early-warning systems integrated into district plans, and LoCAL adaptation planning embedded in government systems with community participation.
claims.limitations: The evaluation reports training and system integration, not comparative district outcomes; recurrent shocks and fragmented funding can weaken continuity.

claims.locator: PDF p.63 (printed p.60), §3.7 Sustainability; PDF pp.63–64 (printed pp.60–61), Finding 18.
claims.paraphrase: Local consultative councils selected 86 climate-adaptive infrastructure projects; the evaluation also reports municipal upkeep of drainage machinery and Chókwè dike maintenance by local authorities.
claims.limitations: Project examples show reported continuity, not a controlled impact evaluation; do not generalize Chókwè performance nationally.

claims.paraphrase: Cabo Delgado's conflict, displacement, climate exposure and resource pressure overlap in Nankumi (Ancuabe), Naminawe (Metuge) and Metula (Pemba); site selection noted host–IDP tension risk.
claims.limitations: The release reports elevated tension risk and resource-access gaps, not observed climate-caused violence or evaluated project impact.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The release links climate exposure and shared-resource pressure with forced host/displaced/returnee co-residence and potential community tensions.

claims.paraphrase: Community-approved plans propose fairer land access, dialogue with government, reforestation, resilient agriculture and small dams, with community-led implementation intended.
claims.scenario: Near-term community plans as described in the August 2026 release; implementation and outcomes not yet evaluated.
claims.limitations: These are approved/planned actions; the release gives no evidence yet on implementation, benefits or effects on tension.

claims.paraphrase: Normal-to-above-normal northern and above-normal central/southern rains caused floods, road disruption and over 100,000 hectares inundated; Massingir Dam reduced impacts in Chókwè, Guijá, Chibuto and Xai-Xai.
geographies: Rovuma, Messalo, Montepuez and Megaruma basins
Zambeze, Búzi, Save, Limpopo, Incomáti and Umbelúzi basins
Maputo, Gaza, Inhambane, Sofala and Manica provinces
institutions: National Directorate of Water Resources Management
claims.limitations: The report states flood and rainfall impacts but does not attribute them to climate change; impacts are not disaggregated by population group.

claims.paraphrase: INGD reports eight anticipatory-action activations across six basins and for a cyclone (Dec 2025–Mar 2026), evacuating 7,214 people and warning about 1.5 million up to five days ahead; volunteers helped first when formal capacity was exceeded.
institutions: Technical Council for Disaster Risk Management
claims.limitations: Aggregated government-reported actions; district-level outcomes and a counterfactual are not provided.

gaps: No inspected source establishes a causal effect of climate hazards on armed conflict or violence; the strongest direct links concern displacement, crop/food insecurity, resource access and potential host–IDP tensions.
UNDP Cabo Delgado fieldwork was conducted in 2023 in Chiúre, Mecúfi and Pemba, with some Metuge interviews; it is not representative of all districts or current 2026 conditions.
The OCHA 2026 humanitarian overview endpoint returned HTTP 403, and the FAO Open Knowledge page returned HTTP 403; neither was used for claims.
Recent government summaries document flooding and anticipatory response, but provide limited population-group disaggregation and no district-level counterfactual evaluation.
The 2026 community spatial plans in Ancuabe, Metuge and Pemba are proposed resilience and resource-governance measures; their implementation and effects on tensions remain unevaluated.
